literal: Limb resembling human likeness is indeed not; highly estimable character resembling is the likeness that is true likeness.
translation: Resemblance in physical limbs is not true human likeness; a similarity in estimable character is the only true likeness.
modern: உடலின் உறுப்புகளால் ஒன்றுபட்டிருப்பது மனிதர்களுக்கு இடையேயான உண்மையான ஒப்புமை அன்று; போற்றத்தக்க நற்பண்புகளால் ஒன்றுபட்டிருப்பதே உண்மையான ஒப்புமையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines what constitutes true similarity among human beings. It states that merely having the same physical limbs does not make people truly alike. Instead, it is the sharing of noble character that forms the true basis of human likeness. The word 'veṟuttakka' is used here in its classical sense of 'highly estimable' or 'abundantly worthy' rather than its modern negative meaning of 'detestable', fitting the chapter's focus on courtesy and good character.
